01 / AI WORK & COST METERING

Office Lab

Same work. Two ways to run it.

Build a manual team and an agent-assisted team. Run a shift, compare the modeled output and follow the AI spend into its records.

  • Change the team
  • Compare cost per brief
  • Inspect & export
Open Office Lab ↗
What’s powered by the SDK?+
  • Oracle ledger

    Stores the sample usage payloads captured with the Rust SDK, linked to a customer and task.

  • Signed transactions

    Preserves the recorded writer, transaction hash and captured signature-verification result.

  • Record queries

    The demo groups those captured calls by brief so you can inspect quantities, charges and exported evidence.

What the application adds

The application supplies the office, task scheduler, sample rates and staffing assumptions. People, agents, completion times and costs are modeled. The hosted browser replays captured SDK records; additional modeled calls create no new signatures.

Why it matters

See how a team could connect AI usage to a customer, a job and a cost, then use that data to decide what to change.

02 / FINANCIAL APPS & SIGNED EXECUTION

Exchange Lab

One order. A trail you can check.

Step into a low-poly trading room. Watch a paper order get signed, verified and matched, then try a trade and inspect its evidence.

  • Watch the walkthrough
  • Try a paper trade
  • Verify a signature
Open Exchange Lab ↗
What’s powered by the SDK?+
  • CLOB matching engine

    The SDK matches compatible orders by price, then time, using the resting maker’s price.

  • Transaction codec & cryptography

    Actual Rust SDK code runs as WebAssembly in the browser to sign, decode and verify each paper order.

  • Signed order exports

    Inspect the original transaction bytes and IDs. The source project includes an offline signature verifier.

What the application adds

The application adds the paper wallet, balances, scripted traders and interface. Coinbase supplies live spot references and market candles in the full demo. Preview prices are illustrative. Trades are paper; this example does not deploy a validator network or settle real funds.

Why it matters

See how SDK modules can sit underneath a financial application, with signed intent, deterministic matching and inspectable transaction data.

03 / ROBOTICS & AUTONOMOUS SYSTEMS

Robotics Lab

Autonomous work. A record you can check.

Follow an autonomous robot from task assignment to verified completion. Inspect signed events, explore operational records and see how the SDK fits into software operating physical systems.

  • Follow a delivery
  • Simulate a failure
  • Test a signed record
Open Robotics Lab ↗
What’s powered by the SDK?+
  • Crypto & Common

    The original Rust SDK signs and verifies each Oracle transaction using the robot’s public demo identity.

  • Oracle ledger & database adapter

    Actual SDK code appends namespaced operational payloads, derives record IDs and queries the application-provided in-memory store.

  • Readback & inspectable evidence

    The application retrieves each stored event, checks it against the signed payload and exports the original transaction bytes. An offline verifier replays the evidence.

What the application adds

The application simulates the warehouse, robot movement, scheduling, battery, failure detection, reassignment and costs. SDK signing, record writes, reads, queries and signature checks execute locally in WebAssembly. Records are session-local. Public demo keys do not authenticate physical devices; signatures do not prove a delivery happened.

Why it matters

See how software coordinating autonomous systems can associate reported work with machines and tasks, preserve signed events and detect edits to the recorded message.

04 / AI INFRASTRUCTURE & OPERATIONS

AI Operations Center

Every agent. Every task. Every dollar.

See how an organization can account for AI activity across departments, agents and customers. Investigate spending, inspect usage records and explore the SDK mechanics underneath.

  • Follow the AI spend
  • Investigate an agent
  • Audit a customer bill
Open AI Operations Center ↗
What’s powered by the SDK?+
  • Oracle records & queries

    Original Rust SDK code records each newly generated usage payload and reads it back from a session-local memory store.

  • Crypto & Common

    Twenty public demo identities sign genuine Oracle transactions. Actual SDK signature checks accept the original and reject an edited local payload.

  • Inspectable evidence

    SDK-generated IDs, signer and signature bytes, original payloads and transaction bytes connect modeled accounting to actual recorded evidence.

What the application adds

The application simulates AI workflows, token quantities, tool use, pricing, budgets, alerts, billing and dashboard analytics. No provider is called. SDK signing, Oracle writes, reads and verification execute newly in browser WebAssembly. Local records clear on restart. Signatures authenticate messages, not external usage or pricing truth.

Why it matters

See how developers can build traceable usage accounting, customer billing and operational monitoring around SDK-backed application records.

05 / FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE & AUTONOMOUS AGENTS

Agent Payment Network

When agents need to pay for work.

Watch AI agents request paid services, authorize transactions and transfer demonstration assets using Nunchi SDK components. Inspect every payment from signed intent to ledger state.

  • Autonomous payments
  • Signed transactions
  • Inspectable accounting
Open Agent Payment Network ↗
What’s powered by the SDK?+
  • Coins ledger & balances

    Original SDK code creates an isolated demo asset and applies signed transfers between agent and provider accounts, with actual nonce and balance checks.

  • Crypto & Common

    Original Rust transaction encoding, signing and verification run as WebAssembly. Altering a local amount fails verification against the original signature.

  • Oracle service records

    A real signed and retrieved service-context record references the payment’s SDK transaction ID and the application request.

What the application adds

The application provides agent behavior, quotes, spending rules, manual approvals, duplicate-request tracking, fulfillment and the interface. All services are fictional. SDK Coins transfers, balances, signatures and Oracle records execute locally in memory. Public demo identities and credits have no real value; no network settlement or production payment security is claimed.

Why it matters

See how developers can combine SDK financial and cryptographic primitives with their own service and authorization systems.
